message.content:
Here’s a concise overview of key Texas traffic laws and regulations you should know: | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph on rural interstates).
• In school zones: 25 mph during school hours; 35 mph otherwise. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 years or weighing < 40 lb must use a child safety seat. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held texting or calling while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal for drivers over 21.
• Zero‑tolerance (0.02 %) applies to drivers under 21. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, vehicles approaching from the right have priority.
• Pedestrians always have priority at crosswalks. | | **Traffic Signal Compliance** | • Red lights mean stop; green means proceed (unless a sign indicates otherwise).
• Yellow lights require safe stopping if possible. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots before changing lanes.
• Passing on the right is only allowed when the vehicle ahead is turning left. | | **School Bus Regulations** | • Stop for all vehicles when a school bus stops to pick up/drop off children.
• Do not pass a stopped school bus until its red lights are off. | | **Parking Restrictions** | • No parking within 20 ft of a fire hydrant, crosswalk, or intersection.
• Parking on sidewalks is prohibited unless marked otherwise. | | **Vehicle Equipment** | • Headlights must be on between sunset and sunrise, and during inclement weather.
• Tires must have adequate tread depth (minimum 2 / 32 in). | | **Insurance & Registration** | • Proof of insurance must be carried in the vehicle.
• Vehicle registration stickers must be displayed on the rear license plate. | ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas 1. **Always obey posted speed limits** – they’re set for local road conditions. 2. **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk or text. 3. **Keep a safe following distance** – the “two‑second rule” works well in most conditions. 4. **Check mirrors and blind spots** before changing lanes or merging. 5. **Stay alert for pedestrians and bicyclists**, especially near crosswalks and in residential areas. If you need more detailed information—such as specific statutes, recent changes, or how to handle a particular situation—just let me know!
